title: Self-Certification of Representation Adequacy: Sequential Certification at Minimum Task Loss
abstract: arXiv:2608.02267v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Agents that act on a compressed representation of their history face a structural risk: if the representation aliases histories with different optimal actions, no rule measurable with respect to the representation can avoid an irreducible per-round loss, and the agent may be unable to detect this from its own transcript. This paper develops a four-layer theory of self-certification of representation adequacy. The static layer defines decision-theoretic adequacy through a Bayes-risk grouping identity and prices a one-shot external verification by an exact total-variation threshold. The sequential layer poses certification as an optimal-stopping problem in the currency of task loss: we define an environment-wise certification complexity constant through a covering linear program, prove an information-task-loss lower bound for every delta-correct strategy, and give a Certification Track-and-Stop policy whose cost matches the bound asymp

translated_title: 表示充分性的自认证：以最小任务损失进行序贯认证
translated_abstract: 基于其历史的压缩表示而行动的智能体面临一种结构性风险：如果该表示将具有不同最优动作的历史混叠在一起，那么任何相对于该表示可测的规则都无法避免每轮不可消除的损失，并且智能体可能无法从自身的交互记录中检测到这一点。本文发展了表示充分性自认证的四层理论。静态层通过贝叶斯风险分组恒等式定义了决策论意义上的充分性，并通过精确的全变差阈值为一轮式外部验证定价。序贯层将认证表述为以任务损失为代价货币的最优停止问题：我们通过覆盖线性规划定义了一个环境级的认证复杂度常数，证明了每个δ正确策略的信息-任务损失下界，并给出了一种“认证追踪与停止”策略，其代价与该下界渐近匹配。
tldr: 本文提出了表示充分性的自认证理论，将认证问题形式化为以任务损失为代价的最优停止问题，建立了信息-任务损失下界，并设计了代价与该下界渐近匹配的认证追踪与停止策略。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a four-layer theory of self-certification of representation adequacy, formulating certification as an optimal-stopping problem in task-loss currency, proving an information-task-loss lower bound, and introducing a Certification Track-and-Stop policy whose cost asymptotically matches that bound.
